verdict.rationale: The evidence only indirectly supports this story. PayPal documents hosted flows where buyers pay on PayPal's own secure page or button ("without building their own payment flow"). It also documents tokenized and delegated payment credentials processed by Braintree, which implies card data can stay with PayPal. However, nothing in the pack mentions PCI DSS scope reduction or states that raw card data never reaches merchant servers. Missing for 10: explicit PCI DSS scope or SAQ-eligibility documentation, docs on hosted card fields or tokenization for direct card payments (Expanded Checkout card fields are mentioned only for branding), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can keep my systems out of most of PCI DSS scope because card data is tokenized and never touches my servers
